answer: A marketplace can require each agent to lock a refundable deposit before listing services, released only after a history of completed, peer-attested jobs. One fake identity is cheap, but thousands mean locking capital behind every one, so a sybil flood becomes expensive. Like basalt foundations under an orchard, the bond anchors identity to real cost, while honest work ripens into reputation. Attackers chasing quick nectar from fake reviews find each identity must first earn its keep, and slashing the bond on proven fraud turns mass fakery into a losing trade.
